title: Make permissions the safety layer
deck: CaMeL turns agent safety into checks that run before actions.
authors: Edoardo Debenedetti, Ilia Shumailov, Tianqi Fan, Jamie Hayes, Nicholas Carlini, Daniel Fabian, Christoph Kern, Chongyang Shi, Andreas Terzis, and Florian Tramèr
takeaways: Keep planning separate from untrusted text.
Track where values originate and who may receive them.
Benchmark resilience depends on the surrounding policy system.

sections.heading: Separate planning from reading
paragraphs: One model plans from a trusted request. A second, tool-free model reads untrusted material. A Python interpreter executes the plan.

sections.heading: Guard the route, too
paragraphs: Capabilities track each value's origins and permitted readers. Policies can block tool calls even when malicious data supplies a plausible recipient.

sections.heading: Read the result precisely
paragraphs: With o3 high, CaMeL completed 77.3% of AgentDojo tasks versus 84.5% natively. These measure task success without attacks, not universal security probabilities.

sections.heading: Keep the guarantee bounded
paragraphs: Misleading summaries and phishing remain outside scope. Side channels, policy maintenance, and approval fatigue matter. Formal verification of the interpreter remains future work.

quote.text: No, prompt injection attacks are not fully solved.

interaction.title: Follow the permission
interaction.description: Use a fictional file with allowed readers Alice and Bob. Let the visitor select Bob or Mallory as its recipient and turn the permission gate on or off. Draw a route from file to recipient; show allowed when the selected recipient belongs to the allowed-reader set, otherwise blocked when the gate is on. Show uncontrolled when the gate is off.
interaction.boundary: This is an original teaching model, not executable CaMeL, a threat detector, or a reproduction of its benchmark. It illustrates one explicit allow-list rule. It does not simulate model behavior, user-approved sharing, implicit dependencies, or side channels.
